chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from 'Umar ibn Hanzalah, who said:
I carried the rabeebah in a small bag until I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and asked him about it. He said: 'All of it is permissible,' and added: 'For it has a rind/skin.'

From him (al-Barqi), from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', who said: 'I wrote to him asking: 'People differ regarding the rabeebah, so what do you think about it?' He wrote back: 'There is no harm in it.'

From him, from Bakr ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had breakfast at my place in Mina, with him was Muhammad ibn Zayd. They were brought sugary treats containing the rabeebah. Muhammad ibn Zayd said to him: 'This is the rabeebah.' He took a piece, dipped it in it, and then ate it.'

key_terms.الرَّبِيبَةُ: Rabeebah: A specific type of dried fruit or nut, often identified as the date stone or a fruit with a hard outer layer, discussed in fiqh regarding its permissibility.
key_terms.صُرَّةٌ: Surrah: A small bag or pouch used for carrying items.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: La ba'sa biha: There is no harm in it (a legal ruling indicating permissibility).
key_terms.لُقْمَةً: Luqmatan: A mouthful or a piece of food.

ai.seo_question: Is rabeebah (dried fruit/nut with rind) permissible to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: These narrations from al-Istibsar clarify the ruling on 'al-rabeebah' (often identified as the date stone or a specific fruit with a protective rind) within the chapter on the hides of dead animals, establishing its permissibility due to its distinct outer layer. The Imam’s casual consumption of it alongside his companion Muhammad ibn Zayd serves as practical evidence (amali) that it is not considered impure (najis) despite being from a dead animal, reinforcing the principle that the rind protects the inner flesh from impurity.
